title: Closed Lakes
statement: A map grid marks water with 0 and land with 1. A lake is a group of water cells joined by shared sides. Return how many lakes are closed: none of their cells is on the border of the map.

answerKey.pattern: Flood the border lakes first, then count the remaining water groups
keyPoints: Search from every border water cell and mark what it reaches
Then scan the grid; each unmarked water cell starts a new closed lake
Mark its whole lake with BFS or DFS and count one
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Search each lake and check if it touches the border: also O(rows · columns)

hints: Which lakes can never be closed?
Any lake with a cell on the border. Remove those first.
Flood from border water, then count connected water groups that are left.
